policy: Favor the newer design; use one-time conversion/archival instead of permanent compatibility. Feature removal is a separate decision, not implied by compatibility policy.
scope: 17 ledger records and 44 explicit preserve groups, with overlaps. Rechecked stated boundaries and traced candidates against current source, not a fresh line-by-line audit. Board-specific directories and mixed-file board behavior excluded. No live data/config usage inventory, external caller inventory, product implementation or runtime restart.

store.observation: Migration returns Ok(false) unconditionally; Store still retains its result.

writer.observation: The inert flag still guards current/catch-up/rebuild selection; those recovery paths remain useful.

cli.observation: Old command aliases remain accepted alongside canonical operations.

keymap.observation: The old runtime name remains a keybinding alias.

invoke.observation: The control dispatcher independently accepts the same alias.

cargo_guard.observation: A resource/UX guard blocks unscoped cargo clean in workspaces explicitly using {cargo-cache-home}; not an OS containment boundary.

cargo_caller.observation: The guard executes before sandbox preparation.

build_scheme.observation: Horizon retired shared build directories and uses independent worktree targets seeded by reflink.

git.observation: The shared shell classifier still serves Git metadata preflight; removing the Cargo guard does not remove this need.

provider_file.observation: The named provider resolver still synthesizes an entry from the legacy [provider] fields.

provider_old_api.observation: The old constructor wraps the named-provider constructor. Production-masked source search found no production call; remaining calls are test fixtures.

provider_adapter.observation: Config DTO to agent DTO translation is a legitimate crate boundary, independent of legacy syntax.

title_endpoint.observation: Title generation directly reads legacy [provider].base_url after the env override.

title_client.observation: The OpenAI-compatible title client caches the first constructed client process-wide.

judge_client.observation: The OpenAI-compatible judge client caches the first base URL/key configuration process-wide.

judge_environment.observation: Session judge construction receives agent_config.rig.base_url; helper routing must be explicit with named providers.

start_identity.observation: Current start events carry a provider call ID without an occurrence ID.

request_identity.observation: Request, approval and approval resolution occurrence identity is optional in published contracts.

result_identity.observation: Results also allow missing occurrence identity.

frame_identity.observation: Absent identity selects a latest preceding call; start events take this path today.

replay_identity.observation: Replay has both occurrence lookup and latest-call fallback, plus a distinct pending provider-call map.

sql_identity.observation: Recall joins permit untagged results and select a preceding request.

halted.observation: Documented legacy-only variant; production source matches found no active constructor.

old_retry.observation: Documented legacy-only variant; old requests fail closed instead of gaining unsandboxed execution.

switch_accept.observation: Daemon validates current config, sends names only, updates stored selection and announces before provider session application.

switch_apply.observation: Provider session resolves again against its own spawn-time tables; application can reject a daemon-accepted new provider.

moa_config.observation: Dedicated named-provider based MoA configuration exists.

moa_pass.observation: Every owner message in a MoA session launches a proposer pass before aggregation; this is more than ordinary task delegation.

moa_host.observation: MoA has dedicated launch/watch and host registration plumbing over shared child-session infrastructure.

session_loop.observation: Command priority, durability and completion ordering remain; task and MoA cancellation lifetimes have different consumers.

history.observation: The loader already prefers supplied JSONL events containing StateChanged or MessageCommitted, before querying DuckDB.

replay_shape.observation: Provider-template pairing repair remains useful even when JSONL is authoritative.

clearing.observation: Canonical history and provider clearing projection retain distinct purposes and provider-call occurrence counting.

candidates.title: Remove inert DuckDB migration state
remove_or_replace: No-op migration function, Store boolean/getter, always-true writer guard and stale documentation.
retain: Current, incremental catch-up and full rebuild; JSONL authority and atomic projection publication.
candidates.migration: None: the migration function already does nothing.
implementation_validation: Existing current/catch-up/rebuild and malformed-record recovery tests; workspace gate.
candidates.remaining_decision_or_unknown: No new feature decision. Do not replace all startup paths with full rebuild without startup-cost evidence.

candidates.title: Keep only canonical command names
remove_or_replace: new-config-agent parser branch and alias-only help/tests/diagnostics.
reload-session-runtime CLI, keybinding and control invoke aliases.
retain: new-agent --role config; reload-agent-runtime; separate internal command and external wire vocabularies.
candidates.migration: Rewrite personal scripts and keybindings once; external usage has not been inspected. No agent/terminal event-format migration.
implementation_validation: Canonical role creation and runtime reload parse/dispatch tests; unknown old names follow the normal error path.
candidates.remaining_decision_or_unknown: Backward compatibility policy is already accepted; no evidence that external aliases are unused.

candidates.title: Retire the obsolete shared Cargo-cache guard
remove_or_replace: tools/bash/cargo.rs including dedicated classifier/tests, its module declaration and sandboxed execution precheck.
retain: Git metadata preflight and shared shell lexer; filesystem authority and OS sandbox.
candidates.migration: No data migration. Workspaces outside Horizon still using {cargo-cache-home} lose this dedicated accidental-clean protection.
implementation_validation: Bash still runs within the same sandbox; Git metadata preflight and approved grants remain covered.
candidates.remaining_decision_or_unknown: Recommend dropping support for this retired Horizon-specific cache scheme; retaining it for other projects is a product choice.

candidates.title: One named-provider configuration form
remove_or_replace: RawProviderConfig/[provider] parsing, conversion and mixed-form precedence branch; legacy-only warnings, constructor and duplicate legacy-name constants.
Update examples, schema-shape tests and test fixture callers to named provider setup. Constants needed for a no-file default may remain under a non-legacy name.
retain: No-file/env-only startup default, env precedence, environment-only secrets, named-provider resolution and crate-local DTO adapter.
Config write TOML validation, mtime check and atomic replacement.
candidates.migration: Translate old model to named-entry default_model and base_url to base_url once; set default_provider. If both forms exist, retain the already-effective named list. Detect residual old syntax explicitly at cutover rather than silently reverting to defaults; no permanent runtime translation layer.
implementation_validation: Named/default/env precedence, absent key behavior, retired config diagnosis, helper endpoint and key selection, sample config parsing.
candidates.remaining_decision_or_unknown: Title/judge are OpenAI-compatible helpers; do not blindly route them to a default Anthropic provider. Proposed explicit named OpenAI-compatible helper selection and client lifetime tied to resolved config; which provider to use and whether C09 is retained remain decisions.

candidates.title: Require execution occurrence identity at publication
remove_or_replace: Optional published occurrence IDs and old latest-preceding-call fallbacks in frame/replay/recall SQL.
Identityless ToolCallStarted payload; update all current producers including mock, synthetic results and approval retries.
retain: Provider call ID separate from execution attempt; pending batch tracking, superseded rows, stale async completion rejection, grant revalidation and retry outcomes.
Internal pre-publication builders may represent incomplete data; never fabricate an unrelated ID to satisfy a type.
Clearing projection has its own provider-call representation; required event IDs alone do not remove its occurrence counting.
candidates.migration: Back up JSONL, convert only unambiguous relationships once while preserving sequence/event identity; archive unresolvable old records separately. Rebuild DuckDB with required identity and verified uniqueness. Bump agent wire protocol, regenerate schema, rebuild and restart app plus agentd. Check shared-contract consumers without expanding into board implementation.
implementation_validation: Reused call ID, multiple retries, stale results, cancel/resume, start/request/result matching, replay/UI/SQL parity, no multiplied join rows; importer preserves originals and rejects ambiguity.
candidates.remaining_decision_or_unknown: Actual legacy record counts/ambiguity unknown; real logs were not read or changed. Historical archive accessibility and any excluded board consumer need explicit cutover coordination.

candidates.title: Remove retired event variants
remove_or_replace: Bare Halted and SandboxDenialRetry contract variants; their legacy-only read/display/rejection arms.
retain: HaltedByIterationCap/HaltedByDoomLoop; actual narrow domain/filesystem/Mach/Git retry grant types and checks.
candidates.migration: Bundle with C05 protocol/data cutover. Never guess the guard behind bare Halted; retain unconvertible records in an original archive. Settle an old pending generic sandbox retry as denied/cancelled, never as new authority.
implementation_validation: New halt reasons and narrow retries still work; legacy importer does not invent guard causes or grant authority; preserved archive and schema gate.
candidates.remaining_decision_or_unknown: Only static production searches establish no visible current constructor; historical occurrence counts and transitive consumers remain implementation inventory work.

candidates.title: Resolve model switches using one config generation
remove_or_replace: Daemon acceptance using current catalog followed by name-only re-resolution against session startup catalog.
Premature model/selection announcements before session application succeeds.
retain: Running turn keeps current config; explicit successful switch affects next turn, role tool restrictions and clearing-window adoption remain.
Ordinary reload does not silently change running sessions; attachment/runtime generation guards remain.
candidates.migration: Pass resolved provider/MoA settings to the session and publish after confirmed application. An alternative is a frozen per-session catalog, but then both listing and validation must expose that same catalog.
implementation_validation: Reload adds/removes/changes a provider, then switch on an existing session; success/failure announcements, no stale display, next-turn timing, role overrides and clearing window.
candidates.remaining_decision_or_unknown: Recommend latest config on explicit switch. This is a source-traced inconsistency, not a new executable reproduction; success acknowledgement adds a seam so net code reduction is unmeasured.

candidates.title: Retire automatic Mixture-of-Agents passes if unwanted
remove_or_replace: MoA config/type resolution, dedicated proposer launch/watch registration, pass/conversation state, model selection arms and MoA-only events/fixtures/docs.
retain: Ordinary task/task_output and shared child observation/termination registry; normal task children survive cancelled turns while reports still have consumers.
candidates.migration: Replace configured MoA selections with a chosen single provider/model; settle proposer sessions and preserve historical pass records at a deliberate format cutover. Inspect shared callers before deleting any host or child registry.
implementation_validation: Ordinary child reports, task cancellation/retention and direct model selection remain; no orphan proposer tasks; history conversion.
candidates.remaining_decision_or_unknown: Usage is unknown. Dropping automatic parallel proposals and aggregation is a real feature loss; ordinary task delegation is not an exact replacement.

candidates.title: Use the existing first-message title without AI refinement
remove_or_replace: AI title refinement call, per-attachment attempted flag, title endpoint resolver and dedicated summarize client/module if call-site audit confirms no remaining consumer.
retain: Existing first-message title fallback, shared title normalization and daemon title updates.
Judge is an independent feature, not implicitly retired with title refinement.
candidates.migration: No destructive title migration required; preserve saved titles. Remove or document retired title-model env knob.
implementation_validation: First message supplies a usable title with no model/key configured; attach/reconnect does not invoke refinement; manual/daemon updates remain.
candidates.remaining_decision_or_unknown: Lose concise AI-generated titles. Removing judge too is a separate option that increases human approval requests; not recommended without a feature decision.

prior_decisions.reason: Reopen legacy syntax and config-generation differences; retain DTO ownership and execution-time grant validation.
Separate runtime lifetimes, transport outcomes and timeout semantics represent current behavior; no obsolete compatibility found at these seams.
Native/WASM capabilities and plugin export visibility are current platform contracts.
Required occurrence IDs can simplify correlation, not durable commit-before-publication or idempotent approval ordering.
Required identities do not eliminate cancellation priority, pending batches or stale asynchronous completion filtering.
Ordered input, bounded query priority and discrete events preserve current terminal behavior.
A timeout cannot undo accepted effects; adding cancellation would need an operation protocol, not deleting a compatibility arm.
Artifact replacement and cancellation ownership prevent a stale preview load from attaching.
Entity-owned publication and teardown avoid stale receipts; no legacy-only branch identified.
Remove aliases only; explicit session targets, close/detach/terminate, restore and focus behavior still differ.
Agent/terminal reload and attachment lifetimes are intentional; terminal priority/caching are not legacy compatibility.
Schema, execution and display make different decisions; the rejected probe is historical evidence, not authorization for further trial features.
Explicit result envelope already centralizes interpretation; no feature removal is justified by this retained boundary.
Retire only identity fallback and generic old retry kind; human/judge freshness checks, grant validation and work tracking remain.
Confinement, atomicity, partial failure and output budgets are current functionality; config file simplification does not remove safe writes.
URL/DNS/connected-IP/redirect checks and secret redaction are security layers; registration guards actual async work.
MoA can be removed by feature choice; task reports and child lifetimes cannot then be blindly flattened.
Config/recall/memory own different data and effects; changing provider syntax does not remove mtime/atomic write requirements. Board memory behavior is excluded.
Reopen process-lifetime helper config premise with named providers. Trusted mediation, escalation fallback and candidate checks remain if judge is retained; removal would increase human prompts.
Mocks are deterministic test fixtures, not obsolete runtime compatibility. Update their event identity to the new published contract.
Remove inert migration flag and plan identity/enum cutover; retain JSONL sequence high-water, turn tracking and acknowledged durability.
Exact identities can simplify result joins; rebuildability, transactions and malformed-record isolation remain.
Reopen model-switch generation/announcement semantics; retain hello, replay subscription, attachment lifetime and shutdown flush.
Remove old command aliases only; framing, identities, socket lifecycle and validation remain real transport responsibilities.
Distinct chooser selection and focus behavior remains useful; no redundant compatibility adapter identified.
PTY lifecycle and subscribe-before-create prevent real races; UI disconnect remains separate from termination.
Wire negotiation and skew detection are the cutover mechanism, not a requirement for old/new runtime coexistence.
Real-process tests intentionally preserve data across restart; production recovery and test retries differ.
Preview artifact/load and guest/host ownership remain current feature boundaries; board registry implementation excluded.
Sandbox authority, excluded-path precedence, credential checks and process cleanup cannot be dropped as old compatibility.
CONNECT, HTTP and tool redirects have different evidence and authority; keeping opaque TLS is intentional.
Optional title refinement can go; native/CLI/WASM routing, panic ownership and title normalization still serve current entrypoints.
Remove retired enum values/identity fallback but retain analytical halted grouping for current guard reasons and durable ordering.
Acceptance, completion and timeout are different current effects; a generic success abstraction would lose information.
Reopen legacy provider syntax and model-switch generation; retain pure file resolution and execution-time grant validation.
Host and guest already share theme interpretation; parse failure and publication lifetimes remain distinct.
Durability before activation and rollback are current ordering guarantees, not backwards compatibility.
No duplicate recovery owner found; timeout and effect cancellation still differ; real OS tests stay.
Restore identity checks and fail-closed persistence prevent current races and data loss.
Reopen generation policy and old config syntax; retain startup/reload failure distinction, env reading and live grant checks.
Keep canonical/provider histories and retry cutoff. JSONL-first normal resume already exists; this is not a new refactor opportunity.
Require occurrence identity without conflating asynchronous Started and final results or discarding failed retry outcomes.
OS capabilities and unsupported-platform denial reflect real security/platform differences; retiring OS support would be a separate product decision.
Keep native-only effects outside WASM; board preview remains excluded.
Keep exhaustive frame reduction and ephemeral sidecars; simplify only occurrence and retired event forms.
Remove inert migration state outside the real current/catch-up/rebuild decision; retain shared store and recovery paths.
Canonical and provider histories serve different purposes; clearing call occurrence counts do not disappear with C05.
Retired Cargo protection can be removed; Git metadata preflight still needs the cohesive lexer and narrow revalidated grants.
Latest-preceding fallback becomes removable only after current producers and historical format cut over; presentation remains separate.
Resolve config/identity and optional MoA scope while retaining lifecycle priority, acknowledged events and ordinary task report lifetimes.
Excluded paths must deny writes before selecting a capability; this is authority, not historical compatibility.
Unsupported-platform fail-closed capability result remains intentional; no claim of new OS runtime verification.
Linux capability checks remain necessary for the current sandbox; no claim of new OS runtime verification.
macOS capability checks remain necessary for the current sandbox; no claim of new OS runtime verification.
Legacy terminal byte encoding is an active external application protocol; removing it would break current terminal clients.
Query priority, input order, synchronized update deadlines and latest-frame publication remain live timing contracts.
Remove obsolete aliases, retain distinct internal command and external control vocabularies.
Watch replacement filtering and cancellation are current preview behavior; no compatibility-only branch identified.
Character geometry represents current rendering behavior; removing it removes glyph support.
Live/history caches and cursor/selection/IME have distinct current geometry and invalidation needs.
Theme role/contrast derivation already has one owner; persistence and live application have distinct effects.

corrections.finding: Normal resume already prioritizes authoritative fallback JSONL events; older replay comments attributing repair to projection lag alone are incomplete. Pairing/template repair still serves current event reconstruction; memory-only board fallback is excluded.

verification.source_provenance: Main target/refactor-audit/sixteenth-final/report.json matches baseline; all 346 production file hashes rechecked. The generated report is local supporting evidence, not required to resolve committed source anchors.
verification.scope_limits: No new behavior experiments, benchmarks, feature usage claims, or implementation correctness claims. Nextest exercises unchanged baseline behavior.
verification.records: Every explicit preserve selector/reason digest and every source anchor/hash is validated against the baseline.
